topics.title: Tiny ponds offer a simple wildlife boost
topics.summary: A gardening writer says even a small container pond can offer water, shelter and food for urban wildlife. The idea makes backyard habitat feel more approachable than a major landscaping project.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could add one tiny nature feature where you live, would you choose a mini pond, bird feeder, balcony herbs, wildflowers, or something stranger? What creature would you hope visits first?

topics.title: Biodiversity summit faces pressure to deliver
topics.summary: Ministers gathering for the COP17 biodiversity summit are confronting slow progress toward targets agreed four years ago. The discussions renew questions about how international nature agreements can turn promises into practical action.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big environmental promise feels far away, what local change seems most real to you: planting native species, protecting parks, changing how food is grown, cleaning waterways, or something else?

topics.title: Finland investigates forest clearing for data-centre site
topics.summary: Finnish authorities have opened a criminal investigation into forest clearing connected to a planned Google data-centre site. The case highlights the tensions between digital infrastructure, permitting and protection of nearby landscapes.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a major new data centre came near your town, what question would you ask first: jobs, energy use, water, forests, taxes, internet benefits, or who gets a say?

topics.title: Toblerone shape dispute reaches court
topics.summary: Toblerone’s owner has sued a small British vegan chocolate maker, arguing that its rounded segmented O'bar too closely resembles the famous Swiss bar’s distinctive design. The smaller company says its product has its own identity.
topics.discussionPrompt: How much can a product’s shape belong to one company? If you invented a snack bar, would you go for a memorable shape, unusual flavour, brilliant name, or eye-catching wrapper?

topics.title: Hidden letters add detail to a historic voyage
topics.summary: A cache of personal letters from a scientist on the ill-fated La Pérouse expedition has resurfaced in France. The letters offer a rare personal view of an ambitious 18th-century scientific journey.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you found a bundle of centuries-old letters in a book, would you read them immediately, preserve them unopened, or hand them to a museum? What history would you most want them to reveal?

topics.title: Autumn light transforms a Scottish landscape
topics.summary: A nature diary from Loch Insh reflects on how Scotland’s shortening autumn days change the quality of light. The piece finds beauty in a seasonal shift often associated with darker evenings.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is the best part of the change into autumn where you are: crisp air, earlier sunsets, bright leaves, cozy indoors, migrating birds, or the excuse for a warm drink?

topics.title: Europe's tech shares slide on AI spending worries
topics.summary: European stocks eased as investors reconsidered the scale and payoff of heavy AI investment. Even so, the broader regional market remained on track for a strong month helped by corporate earnings.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new technology needs huge investment before it pays off, what makes you patient: clear usefulness, exciting possibilities, trusted builders, lower costs later, or a good backup plan?

topics.title: Busy week ahead for markets and central banks
topics.summary: Investors are looking toward US jobs data, large technology earnings, midterm elections and several central-bank meetings. The crowded calendar could offer new signals about growth, inflation and AI investment.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which kind of news feels most connected to everyday life: job numbers, interest-rate decisions, new gadgets, election results, company earnings, or the price of a favorite treat?

topics.title: Data-centre construction raises worker-safety questions
topics.summary: An investigation into Europe’s data-centre building boom reports concerns about working conditions on some projects. The story draws attention to the people and construction work behind the digital services used every day.
topics.discussionPrompt: When you picture the internet, do you think more about apps and devices or the buildings and people behind them? What hidden part of modern technology surprises you most?

topics.title: A major crypto theft renews security debates
topics.summary: A North Korean group has been blamed for a multibillion-dollar theft from Binance, according to reporting on the case. The allegation has put digital-asset security and the risks of online financial systems back in focus.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes an online account feel secure enough to trust: two-step login, a password manager, alerts, backup codes, a helpful human support line, or simply keeping less money online?
